overview: The CC Community Preservation Committee administers local Community Preservation Act funds derived from property tax surcharges and state trust fund matches to support affordable housing, open space, recreation, and historic preservation projects in Medford. The committee's archived meetings cover a timeline extending from March 12, 2018, through November 10, 2026. Over this span, the body has evaluated annual grant applications, established funding set-asides, monitored active capital projects, and executed emergency and small grant recommendations. At its November 10, 2026 meeting, the committee evaluated FY27 proposals for shoreline design and Affordable Housing Trust support, approved an emergency roof grant for the Unitarian Universalist Church, and reallocated lighting funds between municipal parks.

threads.name: Affordable housing and Walkling Court redevelopment
threads.summary: The committee evaluated affordable housing initiatives early in its tenure, reviewing proposals from local housing organizations for multi-unit construction and heating conversions (M02#3, M03#2, M03#3). In late 2022, the Medford Housing Authority presented a multi-million dollar proposal for the expansion and redevelopment of Walkling Court (M11#7). The committee voted to recommend $800,000 in pre-development loan funding for Walkling Court Phase 1 in early 2023, followed by additional construction allocation support later that year (M14#1, M17#3). The committee also expanded housing efforts by recommending seed funding and annual allocations to the newly created Medford Affordable Housing Trust (M24#2, M25#10, M38#2). By mid-2026, construction for Walkling Court Phase 1 was confirmed to begin in late summer 2026 (M33#4).

threads.name: Brooks Estate historic preservation and land management
threads.summary: Preservation and restoration at the Shepherd Brooks Estate emerged as an early focus, covering invasive species control, access drive engineering, stone wall repair, and manor wood trim painting (M02#4, M02#6, M05#3, M05#4). In 2022 and 2023, the committee evaluated further requests for water line testing, access drive design amendments, and exterior envelope restorations (M10#6, M13#12). The body also funded small grant initiatives to design an archaeological protective cap at Thomas Brooks Park (M17#5). In 2026, the committee approved a $10,000 small grant for a desktop archaeological survey covering the estate and neighboring land (M29#1, M35#1).

threads.name: Historic church building restorations
threads.summary: In 2022, Shiloh Baptist Church requested CPA funds to restore historic stained-glass windows, resulting in a recommended $150,000 grant conditioned on a preservation restriction and the exclusion of religious imagery from funded panels (M11#6, M13#2). During the same period, the committee recommended window restoration funds for the historic Isaac Hall House (M11#5, M13#5). Shiloh Baptist Church later secured additional recommendations for ADA accessibility improvements and Phase 2 stained-glass restoration across subsequent grant cycles (M25#9, M29#5, M35#5). In late 2026, the committee evaluated further requests for Shiloh Baptist Church windows and voted to approve an emergency roof grant for the Unitarian Universalist Church (M37#1, M38#3).

threads.name: Condon Shell facility and lighting upgrades
threads.summary: Initial CPA support for the Condon Shell was introduced in 2018 to fund exterior cleaning, masonry weatherproofing, and lighting repair requests (M03#1). In 2023, the committee approved a $3,276 small grant to install electrical outlets and safety lighting for public performances and events (M17#2). Proponents returned in late 2024 with a request for app-controlled field and walkway lighting, which received a recommendation for $98,285 in funding (M24#1, M25#4). In late 2026, to address unexpected construction cost shortfalls, the committee approved reallocating $50,000 from an existing Tufts Park grant to complete the Condon Shell lighting work (M36#4, M38#4).

threads.name: School playground and youth recreation improvements
threads.summary: Recreation requests initially included surfacing replacement at Roberts Elementary School (M02#2). In 2022 and 2023, the committee evaluated and recommended $900,000 across two phases for a universally accessible playground at the McGlynn School (M11#4, M13#4, M17#4). Small grants were awarded in 2024 to install additional play features at Roberts and McGlynn schools while construction on the main inclusive playground neared completion (M20#2, M20#3, M20#4). In 2026, the committee shifted focus to broader youth accessibility by reviewing architectural design studies for playgrounds across three additional elementary schools (M37#4).

threads.name: Municipal cemetery preservation and maintenance
threads.summary: Early cemetery preservation efforts focused on tree replacements and informational kiosk installation at Oak Grove Cemetery (M04#4). In 2022 and 2023, the committee reviewed and recommended funding for perimeter brick wall repairs at Salem Street Burial Ground and a feasibility study for Oak Grove's historic caretakers' quarters (M10#2, M10#4, M13#3). Subsequent cycles yielded recommendations for Oak Grove building preservation design, veteran headstone restoration at Cross Street Cemetery, and system repairs for the Angel of Victory and Peace Fountain (M25#8, M26#1, M28#1, M35#3, M35#4). DPW officials continue to engage the committee on broader master planning and facility options for cemetery structures (M28#6).

threads.name: Small Grants Program policy and expansion
threads.summary: The committee created a Small Grants Program in 2018 to offer a streamlined application pathway for funding requests up to $5,000 (M01#3). The program was sustained with annual reserve set-asides for rolling grant awards supporting park tree inventories and school play equipment (M06#2, M19#2, M20#2). In early 2025, the committee formally adopted policy changes that doubled the maximum small grant award limit to $10,000 and removed mandatory matching requirements (M26#4).

periods.narrative: The committee updated its Community Preservation Plan, established annual budget allocation ratios, and approved major funding commitments for Walkling Court pre-development, the McGlynn School playground, and emergency repairs to the Chevalier Theater.

The committee increased set-asides for affordable housing, doubled the small grant award cap, and recommended over $2 million for City Hall window restorations, historic church preservation, cemetery structures, and seed money for the Affordable Housing Trust.
